_meta.basis: Ingredient quantities are grams PER SERVING of the food as stored (dry dal, raw veg, raw atta) so that nutrition and cost both compute from foods.json without a second source of truth. Scaling to 1-6 people is a multiplication; the app rounds the shopping list, not the recipe.
_meta.why_no_calories_stored: Calories are computed, never typed. A hand-typed kcal that disagrees with the ingredient list is the fastest way to make a tracker lie.

recipes.name: Dal tadka
steps: Rinse the dal and pressure-cook with 3 parts water, a pinch of turmeric and salt - 3 whistles, then let it fall on its own.
Heat the ghee, crackle jeera, add onion and cook till translucent, then tomato till it collapses.
Pour the tadka into the dal, simmer five minutes so it stops tasting like two separate things.
Finish with coriander. Thin it to the consistency you actually eat - that is what the katori measure assumes.
recipes.notes: The cheapest honest protein in the kitchen. Onion is optional this season given the price.

recipes.name: Moong dal with palak
steps: Cook the moong dal soft - it needs less time than toor, about 2 whistles.
Wilt chopped palak in the oil with garlic and green chilli; it loses most of its volume, which is why 100 g raw is one modest katori cooked.
Fold the palak through the dal, simmer briefly, salt at the end.
recipes.notes: Best value protein-plus-iron plate of the Delhi winter.

recipes.name: Rajma masala
steps: Soak the rajma overnight - non-negotiable, both for cooking time and for how it sits with you.
Pressure-cook 20-25 minutes until a bean crushes against the spoon with no resistance.
Brown the onion properly, add ginger-garlic, then tomato till the oil separates.
Add the beans with their cooking water, simmer 15 minutes, mash a few against the side to thicken.

recipes.name: Chole
steps: Soak overnight, cook with a tea bag or amla for colour if you like.
Onion-tomato masala with chana masala powder, anardana if you have it.
Simmer the chana in the masala 15 minutes so they take on colour and salt.

recipes.name: Kala chana sabzi
steps: Soak overnight, pressure-cook till tender but still holding shape.
Temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chilli, toss the chana through dry.
Lemon at the end.
recipes.notes: Cheapest protein per rupee in the whole dataset. Works as a breakfast that doesn't feel like diet food.

recipes.name: Paneer bhurji
steps: Crumble the paneer by hand, not with a knife.
Cook onion, capsicum and tomato down, keep the heat high so nothing stews.
Fold in the paneer for 2 minutes only - longer and it turns rubbery and squeaks.
recipes.notes: Highest-protein veg plate here, and the most expensive. The planner rations it against your budget rather than suggesting it daily.

recipes.name: Palak paneer
steps: Blanch the palak 90 seconds, then straight into cold water - this is what keeps it green instead of khaki.
Blend coarse, not smooth.
Onion-tomato base, add the puree, cook only until it is hot through; long cooking kills both the colour and the folate.
Add paneer cubes at the end.

recipes.name: Soya keema
steps: Soak the chunks in hot salted water 10 minutes, then squeeze dry hard and pulse coarse in a mixer.
Brown onion, ginger-garlic, tomato, then the soya with garam masala.
Add peas and a splash of water, cook covered 8 minutes.
recipes.notes: 40 g dry soya carries ~21 g protein for about eight rupees. The single best lever you have on a Rs 4,000 budget.

recipes.name: Sarson ka saag
steps: Pressure-cook the greens with green chilli, ginger and the radish till completely soft.
Mash with a wooden madhani rather than blending - texture is the whole point.
Thicken with a spoon of bajra or makki flour, cook it out for 10 minutes.
Finish with ghee and a little jaggery if you want it the Punjabi way.
recipes.notes: Dec-Feb only, and worth building a weekend around. Pairs with makki roti.

recipes.name: Aloo gobhi
steps: Cut the gobhi into florets, keep them dry.
High heat, oil, ajwain and jeera, potatoes first for 5 minutes, then gobhi.
Cover and cook on low without water - the steam from the vegetables is enough.
Turmeric, coriander powder, amchur at the end.

recipes.name: Bhindi masala
steps: Wipe the bhindi dry and cut it dry; any water is what makes it slimy.
Fry in a wide pan, single layer, undisturbed for the first few minutes.
Add onion and dry masala once the slime has cooked off.

recipes.name: Lauki chana dal
steps: Soak chana dal 30 minutes.
Pressure-cook dal and cubed lauki together, 3 whistles.
Tadka of jeera, hing, tomato; fold through and simmer.
recipes.notes: Very high volume for very few calories - useful on days you want to eat a lot and stay in deficit.

recipes.name: Baingan bharta
steps: Char the baingan directly on the flame until the skin blisters and it collapses - the smoke is the dish.
Peel under running water, mash rough.
Onion-tomato masala, then the pulp, cook till the water goes.

recipes.name: Poha
steps: Rinse the poha in a colander and leave it to drain - do not soak it.
Fry peanuts, remove, then mustard seeds, curry leaves, onion, potato.
Fold the poha through with turmeric and salt, cover 3 minutes, lemon and peanuts on top.
recipes.notes: Add a katori of curd to make the protein respectable.

recipes.name: Besan chilla
steps: Whisk besan with water to a pourable batter, rest 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped vegetables, ajwain, salt.
Spread thin on a hot tawa, a few drops of oil around the edge, flip once.
recipes.notes: 13 g protein for under twenty rupees. The best cheap breakfast in this file.

recipes.name: Vegetable upma
steps: Dry-roast the suji till it smells nutty and stops looking raw. This is the step people skip and then wonder why it is pasty.
Tadka, vegetables, then 2.5 parts hot water to 1 part suji.
Rain the suji in while stirring, cover, rest off the heat.

recipes.name: Savoury oats
steps: Tadka of jeera and curry leaves, add the diced vegetables.
Add oats, water and milk, cook 5 minutes stirring.
Black pepper, lemon.
recipes.notes: Oats are the priciest grain here at Rs 180/kg. Good food, but on a tight budget poha or suji does similar work for a third of the cost.

recipes.name: Curd rice
steps: Cook the rice soft, cool it to room temperature - hot rice splits the curd.
Mash lightly, fold in curd and grated cucumber, salt.
Tadka of mustard seeds, curry leaves, hing, green chilli.

recipes.name: Moong dal khichdi
steps: Rinse rice and dal together, pressure-cook with vegetables, turmeric and salt in 4 parts water.
3 whistles, then mash slightly for the right consistency.
Ghee on top at the table, not in the pot.
recipes.notes: One-pot, cheap, complete protein from the rice-dal pairing. The default plan filler.

recipes.name: Rajma chaat salad
steps: Use rajma cooked in a previous batch - this is a leftovers recipe by design.
Toss with chopped vegetables, chaat masala, lemon, coriander.
No oil needed.
recipes.notes: Zero-cook, high-protein, high-volume snack. Good answer to 4 pm hunger.

recipes.name: Moong sprout chaat
steps: Soak the moong 8 hours, drain, tie in a damp cloth overnight - by morning it has tails.
Steam 3 minutes if you prefer them soft; raw is fine too.
Toss with chopped vegetables, chaat masala, lemon, coriander.
recipes.notes: Eleven grams of protein for about seven rupees, no cooking. The best thing on this list per rupee.

recipes.name: Roasted chana
steps: Buy it roasted, or dry-roast soaked-and-dried chana in a kadhai till it rattles.
Salt and red chilli. Keep a jar at your desk.
recipes.notes: The answer to 4 pm biscuits. Shelf-stable, so it survives contact with a bad day.

recipes.name: Curd and fruit bowl
steps: Whisk the curd smooth, fold in the cut fruit.
Crushed peanuts on top. A pinch of salt, not sugar - it makes the fruit taste sweeter.

recipes.name: Peanut chaat
steps: Boil the peanuts 15 minutes, or use roasted if you want crunch.
Toss with chopped vegetables, green chilli, lemon, chaat masala.
recipes.notes: Calorie-dense for a snack - the planner uses it on heavy training days rather than every afternoon.

recipes.name: Masala mushroom
steps: Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth rather than washing them - they drink water and then refuse to brown.
Quarter them. High heat, oil, and leave them alone until the undersides colour; crowding the pan steams them instead.
Take them out, then brown onion, ginger-garlic, tomato and capsicum down into a masala.
Return the mushrooms, add turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, and cook two minutes more.
Salt only at the end - salt early pulls the water straight out.
recipes.notes: Mushrooms are mostly water, so 200 g raw cooks down to about one modest katori. Cheap, filling, and barely 50 kcal before the oil goes in.

recipes.name: Mushroom matar
steps: Brown the mushrooms separately first, as always.
Onion-tomato masala, then peas with a splash of water, covered, until tender.
Fold the mushrooms back in at the end so they keep their texture.

recipes.name: Matar paneer
steps: Fry the paneer lightly only if you like it firm, then soak the cubes in warm salted water so they stay soft.
Onion-tomato masala cooked until the oil separates.
Peas and water, simmer ten minutes, paneer in for the last two.

recipes.name: Aloo matar
steps: Cube the potatoes small so they cook in the same time as the peas.
Jeera and hing in hot oil, onion, then tomato until soft.
Potatoes and peas with a little water, covered, until a knife goes through cleanly.

recipes.name: Jeera aloo
steps: Boil the potatoes the day before if you can - cold boiled potatoes hold their shape and crisp better.
Plenty of jeera in hot oil until it darkens, green chilli, then the cubed potatoes.
Leave them undisturbed to catch colour on one side. Amchur and coriander at the end.

recipes.name: Mixed vegetable sabzi
steps: Cut everything to roughly the same size, hardest vegetables in first.
Cook covered on low with no added water beyond what clings from washing.
Dry masala at the end so it toasts rather than steams.
recipes.notes: The catch-all for whatever the fridge is holding. The fridge matcher leans on this one.

recipes.name: Vegetable pulao
steps: Soak the rice 20 minutes and drain - this is the difference between pulao and khichdi.
Whole spices in ghee, then vegetables, then rice, tossed gently for two minutes.
Exactly 1.5 parts water to rice, cover, lowest flame, and do not lift the lid for 12 minutes.

recipes.name: Tofu bhurji
steps: Press the tofu between two plates for ten minutes to drive the water out, then crumble.
Cook the vegetables down hard first.
Tofu in last with turmeric and a pinch of kala namak, which does the egg-like work.
recipes.notes: Same idea as paneer bhurji at a fifth less cost per gram of protein, with none of the saturated fat.

recipes.name: Kadhi
steps: Whisk sour curd and besan with water until there is not a single lump, then pass it through a sieve anyway.
Bring to a boil stirring constantly, or it splits. Once it boils it is stable.
Simmer 25 minutes at least - undercooked kadhi tastes of raw besan.
Tadka of red chilli, methi seeds and hing poured over at the end.

recipes.name: Sambar
steps: Cook the toor dal very soft and whisk it smooth.
Boil the vegetables separately with tamarind and sambar powder so they keep their shape.
Combine, simmer, then tadka of mustard seeds, curry leaves and hing.

recipes.name: Idli
steps: Soak rice and urad dal separately for 5 hours, grind urad first until genuinely fluffy.
Combine, salt, and ferment overnight somewhere warm - in a Delhi winter, inside the oven with the light on.
Steam 10 minutes. A toothpick should come out clean.
recipes.notes: Two days of planning for ten minutes of cooking. Make a big batch of batter; it keeps a week.

recipes.name: Dosa
steps: Same batter as idli, ground thinner and fermented the same way.
The tawa has to be properly hot, then wiped with a halved onion dipped in oil.
Pour from the centre and spiral outward in one motion. The first one is always a sacrifice.

recipes.name: Aloo paratha
steps: Boil and mash the potatoes completely dry - wet filling tears the paratha every time.
Season the filling harder than feels right; the dough mutes it.
Roll gently from the centre, turning as you go, so the filling stays put.
recipes.notes: Two parathas with ghee and curd is comfortably 600 kcal. Worth logging honestly.

recipes.name: Methi thepla
steps: Chop the methi fine and mix it into the dry flours with turmeric, chilli and ajwain.
Bind with curd and only as much water as it needs - methi releases plenty.
Roll thin, cook on both sides with a little oil.
recipes.notes: Keeps two days without refrigeration, which makes it the best thing to carry.

recipes.name: Grilled veg sandwich
steps: Boiled potato sliced thin, cucumber and tomato, a layer of crumbled paneer.
Chaat masala between the layers, not on top.
Grill or toast until the outside is properly crisp.
recipes.notes: Bread is in the packaged list - log two slices alongside this.

recipes.name: Corn chaat
steps: Boil or steam the corn until the kernels pop between your teeth.
Toss hot with butter or a little oil, chaat masala, lemon and the chopped vegetables.

recipes.name: Tomato soup
steps: Cook tomatoes, onion and garlic with a little water until collapsing.
Blend, then pass through a sieve if you want it smooth.
Back on the heat with salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar to correct the acidity.
recipes.notes: Very low calorie for the volume - useful on a day that has already gone badly.

recipes.name: Paneer tikka (home)
steps: Hang the curd for 20 minutes so the marinade clings instead of sliding off.
Marinate paneer and vegetables with besan, ajwain, chilli and garam masala for 30 minutes.
Cook on a very hot tawa or under a grill until the edges blacken in places.
recipes.notes: Home version with a fraction of the oil of the restaurant one, and roughly the same protein.

recipes.name: Sprouts poha
steps: Steam the sprouts three minutes while the poha drains.
Usual poha tadka, fold both through together.
Lemon generously at the end.
recipes.notes: Ordinary poha with the protein roughly doubled for about four rupees more.

recipes.name: Egg bhurji
steps: Cook onion and tomato down first, fully.
Beaten eggs in on low heat, stir constantly, pull off while still slightly wet.

recipes.name: Home-style chicken curry
steps: Marinate the chicken in curd, turmeric, ginger-garlic for 30 minutes.
Brown onions deeply - this is the body of the curry and it cannot be rushed.
Tomato till the oil separates, then the chicken, sear, then water and simmer 20 minutes.

recipes.name: Egg curry
steps: Hard-boil the eggs, peel, and prick them a few times so the masala gets in.
Shallow-fry them with a little turmeric until the skins blister.
Standard onion-tomato gravy, eggs in for the last five minutes only.

recipes.name: Chicken tikka (home)
steps: Two marinades: first salt, lemon and ginger-garlic for 20 minutes, then hung curd with the spices for an hour.
Cook hot and fast - a grill, or a tawa with the chicken pressed down.
Rest five minutes before cutting, or the juices run out onto the board.
recipes.notes: About 56 g of protein per serving. Nothing vegetarian in this file comes close.

recipes.name: Light fish curry
steps: Salt and turmeric the fish, rest 10 minutes, shallow-fry briefly and set aside.
Mustard oil must smoke before anything goes in.
Onion-tomato base thin with water, slide the fish back in for the last 6 minutes only.
